The [language models chapter](language-models.qmd) predicted each next character with a [GRU](rnns.qmd#def-gru),
which carries everything it knows about the earlier characters in one [hidden state](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/cnn-rnn.html#def-hidden-state).
This lecture builds a network that looks back at every earlier character directly:

1.  a weighted average whose weights the network computes from the inputs;
2.  that average applied within one sequence, and the order information it loses;
3.  several such averages side by side;
4.  a block that stacks them with the layers of the earlier chapters;
5.  a [language model](language-models.qmd#def-language-model) built from those blocks, trained on the same text as the [GRU](rnns.qmd#def-gru).

The [attention chapter](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/attention.html) of the DATA 371/471 notes builds the same idea from word vectors, without code.
